variants.molecular_mechanism: RHD c.1153+6T>C (IVS8+6T>C) lies at position +6 of the intron 8 donor splice site. Thongbut et al. 2019 found the variant in 1 of 129 donors with a weak D phenotype and, in a minigene splicing assay, observed significant exon 8 exclusion, although full-length mature transcript was still the predominant product alongside a shorter, exon-skipped transcript. A newer manuscript by Dall'Osso et al. (Haematologica) reports a conflicting minigene result: only the shorter transcript was detected, with no full-length mature mRNA. The variant is therefore documented in multiple independent weak D cases, and both in-vitro assays show aberrant splicing, but they disagree on how severe the defect is. The reference base is given as N in RHeference (RHef00616); T was used, as reported by Thongbut 2019. Absent from gnomAD v4.

variants.molecular_mechanism: c.149-2632T>A is a deep intronic change in intron 1, reported in one patient with a very weak D phenotype (Floch et al. 2022, Transfusion 62:E14-E16). CONFIRMED FROM THE PRIMARY TEXT (Results, 7 Sep 2026). Serology: RBCs typed D-negative by immediate spin but weakly positive (1+ to 2+) by indirect antiglobulin test with all anti-D tested; monoclonal anti-D in the RhD Variant Investigation Kit were reactive at 1+ to 2+ except LHM174/102 and LDM1, which were non-reactive; C+E-c+e+ with no reduced reactivity; direct antiglobulin test negative. Genetics: the sample was hemizygous for RHD, and exon-specific amplification and sequencing of RHD, RHCE and RHAG found no changes from conventional. Mechanism: RHD cDNA analysis from the patient found ONLY transcripts carrying an 80-bp intron 1 sequence inserted between the exon 1 and exon 2 sequences (RHD c.149-2624_2704, i.e. 2624-2704 bp upstream of exon 2) - a pseudo-exon inclusion. The T>A change lies 9 bp into that insert and likely promotes the aberrant splice site; it was confirmed by amplification and Sanger sequencing of 370 bp of RHD intron 1 from genomic DNA. The resulting transcript contains a premature stop codon 30-32 bp into the insert. Evidence is therefore patient-derived transcript characterisation in a single case, with NO heterologous functional assay (no minigene or reporter), which meets neither Tier 1 route. Absent from gnomAD v4. AlphaGenome splicing 0.966; SpliceAI 0.14.

variants.resulting_phenotype: Wild type. Normal D antigen expression from the allele carrying c.1154-31T>C. In the Rui et al. 2023 index donor, genotype RHD(c.845G>A)/RHD(c.149-29G>C, c.1154-31T>C) typed 4+ by gel and 3+ by tube with human monoclonal anti-D; the weak D phenotype was attributable to c.845G>A on the other allele, while the allele carrying c.1154-31T>C encoded normal D antigen.
variants.molecular_mechanism: The reference base at c.1154-31 is T, so the correct notation is c.1154-31T>C. Rui et al. 2023 established this from the locus reference genomic sequence NG_007494.1 for RHD blood group alleles, finding T rather than C at this locus, and noted that other authors had already presented the variation as c.1154-31T>C. The ISBT designation RHD*01EL.37, which lists the variant as c.1154-31C>T among the alleles held responsible for DEL phenotypes, therefore rests on an inverted reference orientation. Several independent lines of evidence show no effect on D antigen expression from this position alone. Fichou et al. 2015 carried out extensive functional analyses of RHD splice site variants and found that c.1154-31T>C alone had no functional impact on splicing, with no documented phenotype. Costes et al. 2017 found by next generation sequencing that the variant is always associated in cis with the missense mutation c.1154G>C on the RHD weak type 2 allele and is in linkage disequilibrium with it, that it can be found alone on the RHD gene as a neutral polymorphism, and that the independent site demonstrates a neutral effect on phenotype whether it carries C or T. Bub et al. 2017 associated weak D expression with c.1154G>C, c.1154-8T>A and c.1154-31T>C acting together rather than with the intronic change by itself. In the index case of Rui et al. 2023, a donor with the genotype RHD(c.845G>A)/RHD(c.149-29G>C, c.1154-31T>C) typed 4+ by gel and 3+ by tube with human monoclonal anti-D, confirmed by family study and PacBio sequencing; the weak D antigen was encoded by c.845G>A on one allele while the allele carrying c.1154-31T>C encoded normal D antigen. The population frequency is out of proportion to the phenotype, at 22.3% by the LOVD3 platform (2577 of 11562) against a DEL phenotype frequency of roughly 0.15% in East Asian populations. The parallel case of c.149-29G>C, formerly RHD*01EL.32, was similarly shown not to cause a DEL phenotype by Kim et al. 2021.

Its functional characterisation comes from McGowan et al. 2024 (Transfus Med Hemother 51:252-264), which placed the intron 2 open-chromatin region into a luciferase reporter in HEL cells: with rs675072A transcriptional activity rose to 242% forward and 146% reverse of the RHD promoter alone, whereas rs675072G gave only minor differences (118% forward, 77% reverse), an approximately 2-fold ENHANCEMENT for the A allele. The same study screened 13 weak D, DEL or D-negative samples with normal RHD exons; GATA1 motifs were intact in 12 of 13 and rs675072 was not the cause in any of them. The one variant attributable to a phenotype was a different change, c.1-110A>C, in a DEL sample.

variants.molecular_mechanism: Disrupts proximal GATA1 binding motif (AGATAA→AGACAA): abolishes erythroid-specific ACKR1 transcription. ACKR1 is uniquely regulated by an erythroid-specific GATA1 site in the proximal promoter. The c.−67T>C mutation eliminates GATA1 binding, silencing expression on red blood cells while non-erythroid expression (endothelium, Purkinje neurons, kidney) is preserved via a GATA1-independent alternative promoter. This dual-promoter architecture makes ACKR1 the paradigm for tissue-specific blood group silencing. Confers complete resistance to Plasmodium vivax merozoite invasion.
variants.validation_cell_line: K562 (human erythroleukemia) CAT/luciferase reporter: T allele drives >100× higher reporter activity vs. C allele; HMEC-1 (human dermal microvascular endothelial): promoter activity similar for both alleles confirming non-erythroid escape; EMSA with K562 nuclear extract: GATA1 shift abolished by C allele, supershift confirmed with anti-GATA1 Ab; Primary patient erythroid cells (flow cytometry); In vitro erythroid differentiation of CD34+ cord-blood HSCs (erythroblasts, reticulocytes)

variants.hgvs_notation_c: GYPB Promoter: GATA-1 binding site at −37 (functional site)
variants.alternative_notation: GYPB promoter GATA element at −37 bp
variants.genomic_region_element_gene: GYPB: Proximal promoter; GATA-1 binding site at −37 bp relative to transcription start site
variants.gypa_gypb_allele_background: N/A (wild-type regulatory architecture; documented by site-directed mutagenesis)
variants.resulting_phenotype: Loss of erythroid GYPB transcription (experimental only)
variants.molecular_mechanism: Mutagenesis of the −37 GATA-1 binding site in GYPB proximal promoter abolishes GATA-1-dependent transcriptional activation in erythroid cells; the −37 GATA site is required for efficient GYPB expression; no clinical variant at this position has been reported

variants.gypa_gypb_allele_background: N/A (wild-type regulatory architecture; documented by site-directed mutagenesis)

variants.molecular_mechanism: Mutagenesis of −75 GATA-1 site with intact ubiquitous site extinguishes GYPB promoter activity; double mutation of both binding sites causes loss of erythroid specificity; hGATA-1 displaces repressor proteins bound at −75 to activate GYPB transcription in erythroid cells
variants.validation_cell_line: Erythroid and non-erythroid cell lines (CAT reporter assay; Rahuel 1992)
variants.be_guide_sequence_notes: Possible CBE guide targeting C→T in GATA site context at −75; MEDIUM feasibility

variants.alternative_notation: GYPB E-box −70; USF1/USF2 and ubiquitous factor U binding
variants.genomic_region_element_gene: GYPB: E-box sequence at −70 bp in distal promoter; binds USF1/USF2 (activating) and ubiquitous repressor factor U (repressing in non-erythroid cells)
variants.resulting_phenotype: Loss of erythroid-specific GPB expression; ectopic GPB expression in non-erythroid cells (experimental)
variants.molecular_mechanism: E-box at −70 is occupied by both USF (activating) and factor U (repressing); mutagenesis impairing factor U binding leads to GYPB expression in non-erythroid cells (loss of erythroid specificity); along with Ku70, this E-box represses GYPB in non-erythroid contexts
variants.validation_cell_line: Erythroid and non-erythroid cell lines (CAT reporter; cotransfection; Camara-Clayette 1999)
variants.be_guide_sequence_notes: E-box CANNTG: if a C→T edit in editing window disrupts E-box → possible; MEDIUM feasibility
variants.bystander_edits: E-box disruption may have pleiotropic effects

variants.hgvs_notation_c: GYPB IVS3 5' splice site inactivating mutation (evolutionary; pseudoexon B silencing)
variants.alternative_notation: GYPB intron 3 (former intron 3 of ancestral GPA gene) splice site loss; pseudoexon B silence
variants.genomic_region_element_gene: GYPB: Intron 2/3 boundary (pseudoexon B region); inactivating point mutation at ancestral 5' splice site of GYPA intron 3 homolog that silences GYPB pseudoexon inclusion
variants.resulting_phenotype: Pseudoexon B (GYPB intron 2 region) excluded from normal GYPB transcript: required for correct GPB expression
variants.molecular_mechanism: GYPB evolved from GYPA by Alu-mediated recombination; in this process, a point mutation arose at the 5' splice site of GYPB intron 3 (corresponding to GYPA exon 3 donor) that inactivates 5' cleavage → exon 2 directly ligates to exon 4 in GYPB, skipping the pseudoexon; when hybrid alleles (GP.Mur, etc.) incorporate this region, the splice site context changes and the pseudoexon can be included
variants.population: Universal (present in all normal GYPB alleles)
variants.be_guide_sequence_notes: Evolutionary/constitutive feature: base editing N/A
variants.key_reference: Kudo 1989, Proc Natl Acad Sci USA (PMID 2734312)

variants.alternative_notation: IVS3-8C>T + IVS5+5G>T; near-splice and donor site mutations
variants.genomic_region_element_gene: GYPB: Two intronic changes: IVS3 acceptor at -8 (c.137-8C>T) plus IVS5 donor at +5 (c.270+5G>T); also c.143C>T (exon 4, p.Thr48Met)
variants.molecular_mechanism: Combined near-splice acceptor change at IVS3−8 and canonical splice donor change at IVS5+5; the IVS3 change (-8 position) may further impair exon 4 definition in conjunction with the IVS5+5 mutation → exon 5 skipping → S-U+var phenotype
variants.be_guide_sequence_notes: G→T at IVS5+5 is transversion; C→T at IVS3-8 is CBE-feasible but companion G→T is not: combined correction not feasible
variants.key_reference: ISBT MNS Working Party 2023 (allele table v5.7)

variants.alternative_notation: Exon 16 ESE synonymous Gly573= causing exon 16 skip
variants.genomic_region_element: Exon 16, position +16 from 3' splice site (~ESE context; 16 bp downstream of intron 15/exon 16 junction)
variants.resulting_phenotype: Ko (silent KEL allele): causes Kmod when compound heterozygous with second mod allele
variants.molecular_mechanism: Synonymous substitution p.Gly573= disrupts exonic splicing enhancer (ESE) in exon 16; complete exon 16 skipping confirmed by cDNA analysis; exon 16 skipping → frameshift → truncated protein; all Kell antigens absent

variants.molecular_mechanism: No deep intronic KEL variants causing aberrant splicing have been published as of 2024; known K0 alleles all involve ±1/±2 canonical splice sites or near-canonical ±5 positions; systematic deep intronic sequencing of KEL has not been performed in large cohorts

variants.genomic_region_element: Kpa/Kpb regulatory context: KEL exon 8 flanking introns (intron 7 and intron 8)
variants.resulting_phenotype: No Kpa-specific regulatory variants known; splice variants in introns 7-8 (KEL-NC-005, NC-006, NC-007 in prior table) cause Ko abolishing all antigens including Kpa/Kpb
variants.molecular_mechanism: Kpa (KEL3) is defined by p.Trp281Arg (c.842T>C) in exon 8; no distinct regulatory variants selectively modulating Kpa vs. Kpb expression have been identified; IVS7 and IVS8 splice variants already documented in prior table cause K0 (complete null) rather than selective Kpa/Kpb antigen modulation
variants.be_guide_sequence_notes: N/A

variants.genomic_region_element: Jsa/Jsb regulatory context: KEL exon 17 flanking introns (intron 16 and intron 17)
variants.resulting_phenotype: No Jsa/Jsb-specific regulatory variants known; IVS16+1G>A (KEL*02N.31, prior table NC-011) causes Ko abolishing all Kell antigens; Jsa (KEL6) frequency ~19.5% African Americans: alloimmunization risk to Jsb is clinically significant in this population
variants.molecular_mechanism: Jsa (KEL6) defined by p.Pro597Leu (c.1790C>T) in exon 17; no distinct regulatory variants selectively modulating Jsa vs. Jsb expression are known; IVS16 splice site (NC-011) causes exon 16 skipping and K0 without specific effect on the Jsa/Jsb polymorphism at codon 597; promoter variants (NC-013/014/015) reduce all KEL expression including Jsb
variants.be_guide_sequence_notes: N/A
variants.key_reference: Höher G 2020, Genet Mol Biol (PMID confirmed via PMC7263432); research gap for Jsa-specific regulation

variants.hgvs_notation_c: KLF1 heterozygous loss-of-function (trans-regulatory; not a KEL gene variant)
variants.genomic_region_element: Trans-regulatory via KEL promoter KLF1 binding site
variants.grch38_coordinate: chr19:12,997,047 (KLF1 gene): affects KEL at chr7:142,976,000
variants.kel_allele_background: Any KEL allele (trans effect on ALL KEL alleles)
